title: Mariner Security on-prem deployment scratchpad
content:
Meeting notes (10/14/2025) - intake call with Mariner Security (ops + infra)

Attendees: Marcus (Redwood SE), Ava (Redwood Solutions Eng), Samir (Redwood Infra), Jason Lee (Mariner CTO), Priya Rao (Mariner Ops), Theo Martinez (Mariner Sec)

Purpose: quick scoping call for pilot on-prem deployment of Redwood Private behind Mariner's corporate network and HSM-backed key management. Mariner goal is low-latency rule-based detections in a sidecar pattern and strict data residency.

High-level asks from Mariner:
- Air-gapped option: initial pilot will be in a closed colo (no outbound internet).
- HSM/KMS integration: AWS CloudHSM currently used; but colo has a Thales HSM appliance. They want Redwood to support an HSM-backed key store for model encryption and logging encryption keys.
- Sizing: expect 6-8 concurrent inference streams, models: 13B quantized + 7B for fallback. Prefer NVMe-backed caching. Target p95 latency <250ms for short (<256 token) requests.
- Audit requirements: immutable audit logs for token-level events retained 13 months.
- Upgrade window constraints: maintenance only on weekends 00:00-06:00 local time.

Technical constraints / gotchas noted:
- No internet egress from compute VLAN. Control plane must be able to operate either via a customer-managed proxy with allowlist OR via an offline bundle install. Action: confirm whether Mariner will provide a proxy or we do bundle.
- KMS/HSM: Thales supports PKCS#11. Our current KMS shim has a PKCS#11 adapter but hasn't been tested with this exact model of Thales. Need to do adapter testbench. Risk: different key wrapping semantics -> may require a small connector patch.
- Kernel/GPU drivers: Mariner rack uses A100S w/ a custom OS image (RHEL8 derivative). SRE note: driver versions are slightly older (cuda 11.6). We need to validate our compiled kernels and quantization libs against that driver.
- Container runtime: they run crun and runc variants; OCI hooks for device-plugin exist but kubelet is slightly customized. Potential privilege/security constraints to request GPU mapping. Plan: bring small test daemonset to validate device plugin privileges.
- Networking: internal NTP and a private CA; our TLS cert stack must be installable against their CA chain.

Initial architecture proposal (sketch):
- Private control plane image bundle installed in offline mode (airgap-install.sh) -> customer-run. Control plane runs in a separate management VLAN with egress to internal ops tooling only.
- Serving nodes in compute VLAN (k8s worker nodes). Each worker runs rwd-inference-runtime as a DaemonSet with device-plugin for GPUs and NVMe cache mounted.
- KMS connector: rwd-kms-proxy deployed as a sidecar to control plane components, configured to use PKCS#11 shim pointing at Thales appliance (on a management network). Keys never leave HSM, we store key references in encrypted vault.
- Audit aggregation: local ELK stack forwarder to their SIEM; we must produce structured audit JSON compatible with Splunk/QRadar.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Marcus: send onboarding checklist + airgap installer draft (10/16/2025).
- Samir: run PKCS#11 adapter test against Thales evaluation emulator we have and report compatibility gaps (10/20/2025).
- Ava: prepare minimal device-plugin daemonset example for their kubelet flavor; include GPU mapping troubleshooting steps (10/18/2025).
- Mariner (Jason): confirm whether they can provide outbound proxy for control plane telemetry or prefer fully offline install (due 10/17/2025).
- Priya (Mariner Ops): share inventory: kernel version, cuda driver version, exact Thales model, NVMe topology (10/17/2025).

Open questions / risks we need answered:
- Can they accept a short-lived management VPN tunnel for initial control plane bootstrap (temporary, customer-initiated)? If yes, simplifies metrics and updates.
- Audit retention length is 13 months — need to verify storage sizing and whether compression/rollup acceptable.
- Model licensing: will they permit us to ship quantized model artifacts, or must we provide a model build pipeline for them to run locally? Clarify legal/ops.

Notes to self:
- Bring up offline install docs we used for previous customer (private-deployments/pilot-bundle-2025) and remove any AWS-specific references.
- Test NVMe cache performance with cold-starts for 13B quantized model under cuda 11.6 (likely larger memory pressure); might need to recommend mixed-precision profiles.
- Prepare a short demo script that runs entirely offline (no telemetry) to show p50/p95 numbers.

Next steps (this week):
- Draft pilot proposal (scope, success metrics, timeline, SLA, rollback plan) and share with Mariner execs and legal (Marcus/Ava) by 10/16.
- Spin up PKCS#11 emulator job and run adapter test (Samir) by 10/20.
- Schedule follow-up technical deep-dive with Mariner infra team (90m) target 10/21; invite infra + security + platform engineers.

Relevant links and references:
- internal: https://confluence.redwood/integration/mariner-onprem-brief
- engineering notes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deployments/pull/278 (airgap installer draft)
- jira ticket: JIRA-8132

Random fragments / brainstorms (notes to self):
- Could offer a "connector appliance" option: small validated jump-box appliance with preinstalled drivers that Mariner can plug into their rack to simplify driver mismatch. Cost: one-time appliance fee.
- Consider a compressed audit export (monthly) that we sign and ship to their long-term store to reduce live retention burden.
- If KMS integration looks risky, fallback: use customer-managed disk encryption with keys rotated in HSM and Redwood only storing sealed keys.

End of scratchpad. This is intentionally rough — convert to a tidy pilot proposal doc once blockers (PKCS#11, driver validation) are cleared.
